# Mine — test requirements

What has to be checked before a change ships, and how. [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) says
what the apps do; this says how we find out whether they still do it.

There is no CI and no test framework. `test/run.sh` drives a real browser against the real app
and prints one line per check, so running it is the whole of it:

```
test/run.sh                 the checks
test/run.sh --shot DIR      the checks, and a screenshot of each view into DIR
```

It needs `chromium` and node 20 or newer on the PATH, installs nothing, and writes nothing into
the repo. A failing check prints what it got and what it wanted, and the script exits non-zero.

## Why a browser and not unit tests

Almost everything that has actually broken here is a layout or a wiring fault — a grid track
that will not shrink, a button that stops being wired when its markup moves, a key written into
the frontmatter that should have been left out. None of those show up in a function test. The
model arithmetic that *is* worth testing in isolation (dates, sprints, recurrence expansion) is
pure and lives in `calendar/data.js`, whose `buildModel` takes files rather than reading them,
so it can be exercised from node against the same markdown the browser mirrors.

## How the harness works

`test/serve.py` serves the working tree, plus one synthetic route, `/__fixture.json`: a month of
entries generated for *the month the checks run in*. A fixture pinned to a fixed date would
leave the month view empty and every check green. It holds what has historically broken things —
long titles, timed entries, a day with more entries than a phone cell shows, all-day items, a
Saturday task.

`test/check.mjs` connects to Chromium over the DevTools protocol, seeds that fixture into
IndexedDB with a throwaway config, and drives the app by clicking the real buttons.

Two things about it are deliberate and easy to get wrong:

- **The viewport comes from `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`, never from `--window-size`.**
  Chromium's headless mode lays the page out at a fixed 500 px and then *scales the capture* to
  the window size, so a 320 px screenshot taken with `--window-size` is a picture of a 500 px
  layout. It passes a fit check that a real phone fails. This cost an afternoon once.
- **The config holds a fake token.** The mirror is local, so every view renders from it; the
  push fails and writes a line into the sync indicator, which is correct and is not a failure.
  Nothing in the checks talks to GitHub, and no real token ever goes near a browser profile.

## What is checked

**Every view fits a phone.** Day, week, month, year and kanban, at 320 and 360 CSS px, in light
and dark. The test is `scrollWidth === clientWidth`: nothing may extend past the screen, in any
view, at any width. 320 px is the floor because it is the narrowest phone still in use and it
leaves room for Android's display-zoom setting, which makes a wider screen behave like a
narrower one.

This is the check that earns its keep. The month grid once ran 1239 px wide at a 360 px
viewport, and it looked perfect on a desktop the whole time: a `1fr` track is
`minmax(auto, 1fr)`, and a cell holding a `white-space: nowrap` title has that whole title as
its minimum width, so seven cells grew to fit their text rather than sharing the screen. A grid
cell that holds text needs `min-width: 0` or it does not shrink. The other offender was the
period label in the top pane, which is long enough in the week and sprint views to overflow a
narrow phone on its own.

**An existing entry opens read-only.** That clicking one — in a grid, in the day preview and as a
card on the board alike — opens a popup containing **no input, select or textarea at all**, and
that its top row runs trashcan, pen, `x` with no disk in it. That the type is shown as something
not pressable. That **only the fields that are set appear**: an entry with a title and a date
renders no location row and no alerts row, which is the check that stops the preview quietly
becoming the form again. That the pen opens the edit popup, and that a `+` or a click on empty
space opens the edit popup directly with no preview in between.

**The shared renderer, where the preview uses it.** That a details body holding `## Agenda`, a
`- ` bullet, a `- [x]` and a `- [ ]`, `**bold**` and a link renders as a heading element, a list
with a ticked and an unticked box, a bold element and an anchor whose href is the link's — and
that a `javascript:` URL in the same body produces no anchor at all. That a body containing
`<script>alert(1)</script>` puts that text on the screen and adds **no script element to the
document**: the renderer builds nodes and never markup, and this is the check that keeps it so.
That a ticked checkbox in the preview is not pressable.

**The entry popup's icon row, toggle row and field rows.** That the edit popup's icon row holds
icons alone, with no letter anywhere in it, and that it holds nothing but the type pair and the
three on the right — task, event, then delete, save, close — with no field icon and no dash left
in it. That **the type pair is disabled on an entry that already exists** and enabled on a new
one, resolved from the buttons' disabled state and not from how they look.

**That the `x` is the rightmost control in every popup**: the entry popup, each of the six field
sub-popups, the day preview and the settings panel. Resolved from the buttons' left edges, so a
row that reads correctly but was built in the old order cannot pass — and a check that only
counted three buttons would have passed on the old order, which is why this one reads their
positions. That the entry popup's and a sub-popup's trio runs trashcan, save, `x` in that order.

That a new entry is an event and its toggle row holds `24h` by itself; that choosing a task puts
stage, important and estimate on that same row and switching back to an event takes all three
away again. That stage cycles through three stages in three badge colours and back; that
**important is a toggle and not a cycle** — two taps return it to where it started, it carries no
badge and no digit, and there is no third state to reach; and that the estimate opens a popup
prefilled with one day, badges `3d` once set and loses its badge once cleared. That `24h` and `!`
light with the ordinary enabled background and never with `--good`, because green is the save
button's, and that nothing else in the popup lights at all. That the row sits **below** the start
and end fields, not above them — resolved from the elements' document order, since a row that
merely looks right can still be the old one.

That the six field rows read details, category, repeat, alerts, location, participants, in that
order on a task and on an event alike, each one carrying its icon and its name; that every field
has a row whether it is set or not; that setting one moves its row above the unset ones while the
order inside each group stays canonical; that a set row shows the field's value and no pen; and
that a set row carries no enabled background, because position and value are what say it is set.

**A repeating entry, which the fixture now carries.** Nothing in it repeated before, so the
scope pair, the skip and the override paths had no entry to run against at all. That the preview
says the entry repeats and carries `skip this one`, and that the **scope pair is not on it**.
That switching scope and then leaving **asks nothing**: switching rebuilds the draft from the
other file, so it has to rebuild the baseline a discard is measured against too — a baseline left
behind reads as undefined, which makes every way out of the popup ask about changes nobody made.

**Discarding asks once, and only when there is something to lose.** That the `x` on a popup
nothing has been typed into closes it with no prompt; that changing a field and then pressing the
`x`, clicking the backdrop or pressing Escape each raise the same prompt; and that **keep
editing** leaves the popup open *with the change still in it*, which is the half of a discard
dialog that usually goes wrong. That ticking **don't ask again** and reopening a popup makes the
next `x` discard without asking, and that the settings panel's `Confirm discard` row turns the

**The settings panel.** That its nine rows are two halves — every label's box in the left half

the one measurement that separates the new panel from the old. That no label wraps to a second
line at 320 px. That **groups are not listed in the panel**: it holds one *edit groups* button,
which opens the same list the category field opens, and that **only this way in carries the pen,
the trashcan and the `+ add`** — reached from an entry the same list has none of the three and no

explanation**.

**The popup is centred.** At 320 px, that the entry popup, a field sub-popup, the settings panel
and the day preview each sit clear of the bottom edge — their bounding box's bottom is above the
viewport's, and their top below it. Nothing in the app is a bottom sheet any more, and a card
that still stretches to the bottom edge is the old sheet in new paint.

**The filter.** That the groups are behind a dropdown rather than listed: the filter popup shows
one `groups` row, and the checkboxes — one per group, each with its colour — appear only once it
is opened. That ticking two of them still shows two groups and hides the rest, because folding
the list away must not have made the filter single-select. That on the board the filter adds an
assignee and **one** important toggle, and that no `P1`, `P2` or `P3` chip is left anywhere in it.

**The top pane.** That it holds no Today button, no `+`, and no `-` or `+` zoom pair — the two
zoom buttons are gone, and a check for their absence is what keeps them gone. That **clicking the
label walks the zoom** year → month → week → day → year, round the cycle, with nothing disabled
at an end. That on the board clicking the label opens the sprint list instead and does not zoom.
That the **caret is a button of its own** and opens the picker, and that clicking the label does
not open it. That the board icon reaches the kanban and is a calendar icon there, returning to
the month view, and that the home icon leaves for the Mine tile screen. That the label reads
`NOV/26`, `W47/NOV`, `FR 20/NOV`, `2026` and `7` in the five views, and that the week label keeps
its ISO number with *show calendar weeks* off.

**The pane's order and its phone layout.** That on a desktop the controls run board, filter, then
the centred period group, then settings and home — read from their left edges, so a reordering
that looks right but wires the wrong button cannot pass. That at 320 px the pane is **two rows**:
board, filter, settings and home share the first with their bounding boxes on one line and none
dropped, and `‹`, the label, the caret and `›` share the second. That the four on the first row
are of equal width, and that the label on the second is **wider than either arrow** — which is
the whole reason the second row exists, so a layout that splits the pane but leaves the label
narrow has not done the job. That **no horizontal swipe does anything**: the same gesture on the
label, on a grid and on the board leaves the period, the sprint and the layout exactly as they
were.

**The month fills the window.** That the month grid's bottom edge reaches the bottom of the
calendar window — within a pixel or two of the sync line above the viewport's end — rather than
stopping at the height its cells happen to need, and that it does so at 320 px and on a desktop
alike without the page gaining a vertical scroll. That a cell still shows at most four lines on
a desktop and two at 320 px: the rows got taller, the cap did not change.

with no `…` — resolved from the computed `text-overflow` and the line's width against the
cell's, not from a screenshot. One-tap done must still be there in the week grid, the day grid
and the day preview.

**The year view.** That clicking a day opens the day preview, and that clicking a month's name
zooms into the month view showing the month that was clicked — not the month the anchor happened
to be in.

**The day view has no day header.** That the day view renders the all-day strip and the hour grid
and nothing above them, and that no element in it carries the weekday-and-date pair the top pane
is already showing. That the **week** view still has its seven, and that clicking one still opens
the day preview — the same check must come out the other way in the two views, or a rule that
removed both would pass as one that removed one.

making the disabled one look live; that a sideways touch gesture on the board changes nothing; and
that a column header's `+` opens a new task in that stage. That the
header carries **no card count and no colour dot**, and that the stage name is drawn in its own
stage colour — red, yellow, green — resolved against the same table the cards use.

**The kanban on a desktop.** That a column header has no `‹` `›` at all, since every column is on
screen, and that **a card has none either** — the stage is changed by dragging. On a phone the
card keeps its pair, so the same check must come out the other way at 320 px.

**What a card holds, and what it no longer holds.** That a card's top row is the title alone,
with a `!` in front of it when the task is important and nothing in front of it when not; that
the `!` is **not a button** — no element bearing it is pressable; and that the card carries **no
pen, no trashcan, no estimate, no sprint number and no priority chip**. On a desktop the card
holds no pressable element at all, and on a phone only the two stage arrows: the count is what
keeps the removed controls removed, since each of them came back once as a chip.

**Clicking a control on a card does not open the ticket.** That tapping the phone's `<` or `>`
moves the card and leaves the entry popup closed, and that clicking the card's body does open it —
the view popup, with no input element in it.

one of its buttons, so both happened at once; it must be written so that a handler that stops at
the button but lets the event bubble turns it red.

**A save is green and a trashcan is red**, in the entry popup, a field sub-popup and the groups

content.content:
# Mine — technical requirements

How [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) is built. Everything here was verified against the live
API or on device on 2026-11-19; `spike/` re-runs the device checks and needs no token.

## Repos

| Repo | Visibility | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maximilianharr/mine` | public | this app, served by Pages at `/mine/` |
| `maximilianharr/mine-data` | **private** | the markdown data |

Pages cannot serve a private repo without Enterprise, so data in the app repo would be
world-readable at a predictable URL. The token is scoped to the data repo only.

## Layout

One `manifest.json` with `scope: /mine/`, one service worker at the root. Subfolders are ordinary
pages inside that scope. `/mine/` and `/mine/calendar/` are the same origin, so they share one
IndexedDB — that is the whole mechanism behind "enter the token once".

```
/index.html /manifest.json /sw.js
/shared/  apps.js  store.js  github.js  md.js  markdown.js  prefs.js  vendor/
/calendar/  index.html  app.js  data.js  ui.js  views.js  kanban.js  popup.js  settings.js
            style.css  icon.svg  sample/
/test/    run.sh  serve.py  check.mjs
```

No build step: no bundler, no CI, no node_modules. `git push` deploys, every page opens from
disk, all paths relative so the `/mine/` prefix needs no config.

The checks in `test/` hold to the same rule: `run.sh` drives a headless Chromium over the
DevTools protocol with nothing installed, and what it covers — and the two mistakes that make
it lie to you — are in [TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md](TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md).

`shared/apps.js` exports the app list and is imported by both the tile screen and `sw.js`, so
adding an app means editing one array. An app may export `summary()` from `widget.js`.

`shared/md.js` and `shared/markdown.js` are two different jobs and stay two files. `md.js` is the
file envelope — it parses and serialises frontmatter and is imported by the paths that read and
write the repo. `markdown.js` renders a body for the screen and is imported only by UI, so nothing
on the file-IO path pulls a renderer in. It **returns a DOM node and never a string of HTML**, which
is what makes a body carrying a `<script>` tag harmless without a sanitiser to get right; what it
covers and why it is hand-rolled rather than vendored is in
[REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md#markdown-bodies).

## Bootstrap — 1 request

One GraphQL query returns an app folder's tree **with contents and blob SHAs**, nested to the
depth of the layout:

```graphql
repository(owner:$o, name:$r) { object(expression:"main:calendar") {
  ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
    ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
      ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
        ... on Blob { oid text isTruncated } } } } } } } } } } }
```

- `rateLimit.cost` is **1** however many files return — `entries` is not a paginated connection.
  A 16 MB / 145 file response came back in 6 s without error.
- `Blob.oid` is byte-identical to the REST tree SHA, so this single request also supplies the
  SHAs that pulls diff against and writes send as their base.
- Check `isTruncated`: GraphQL truncates very large blobs and returns `text: null` for binary.
  Fall back to a REST blob fetch for that path.
- An **empty repo** returns `object: null` rather than an error, and `defaultBranchRef: null`.
  Treat it as an empty mirror, not a failure.

**Do not use the tarball.** `GET /tarball/{ref}` 302-redirects to `codeload.github.com`, which
answers `access-control-allow-origin: https://render.githubusercontent.com` — one specific
foreign origin. `fetch()` applies CORS to the final response after the redirect, so it is
blocked, and the preflight an authenticated request needs returns 403. `api.github.com/graphql`
by contrast sends `allow-origin: *` and a 204 preflight allowing `Authorization`.

**A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright.** Not just the ref read — `POST
/git/blobs` itself answers 409 "Git Repository is empty", so there is nothing to build a tree
from. Only `PUT /contents/{path}` can create the first commit. The first queued file goes that
way, and everything after drains normally once a history exists.

## Pull

1. `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{branch}` with `If-None-Match`. A 304 means nothing changed and
   costs no rate-limit quota.
2. On 200: fetch the tree, diff blob SHAs, fetch only changed files, drop deleted paths.

Run on app open and on window focus. Background Sync does not exist in Safari, so all syncing is
foreground.

## Writes — one commit per drain

Queue each change locally with the blob SHA it was based on, then drain the whole queue as one
commit via the Git Data API: `POST /git/blobs` per file, `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`
(deletion = entry with `sha: null`), `POST /git/commits`, `PATCH /git/refs/heads/{branch}` with
the expected old SHA and **no force**.

One drain is one commit, so a move — delete plus create, because the date is in the path and the
API has no rename — cannot be half-applied, and a 20-item offline backlog is one commit.

A rejected ref update means someone pushed elsewhere: pull, rebuild on the new base, retry. This
succeeds, because nearly every write is a create at a freshly generated path.

**True conflict** = a queued change whose base SHA no longer matches the remote blob. Remote keeps
the canonical path; the local version is committed beside it as `<name>.conflict-<yyyymmdd>.md`
with `conflictOf:`. Nothing is discarded and the queue never jams. On 401/403, pause and send the
user to settings.

## Service worker

Registered `{type: 'module'}` so it can import `shared/apps.js`. A version constant names the
cache; install precaches the shell. Same-origin requests are cache-then-revalidate.

Requests to `api.github.com` **bypass the worker entirely** — caching an API response would hand
back a stale ETag and silently break sync.

A new worker waits; the UI offers "Update ready — reload" and `skipWaiting()` runs only on tap.

**The offer is gated on the version, not on a worker waiting.** The worker answers a `version`
message over a `MessageChannel` port with its `VERSION` constant, and the page compares the
waiting worker's answer with the active one's; equal answers mean no banner. A worker that is
byte-identical to the running one can sit in `waiting` indefinitely, and `reg.waiting` alone as
the condition is what makes the banner appear on an app with no update and never go away. A
worker too old to answer reports `null` after a 1.5 s timeout, which differs from a real version
and so still offers the update.

## Token and CSP

Stored plaintext in IndexedDB with its expiry: as safe as the unlocked device. The threat that
matters is injected script on our own origin, closed off by policy rather than encryption:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com
```

**No CDNs, ever.** Dependencies are committed to `/shared/vendor/`, pinned by hand, with source
URL and version in `VENDOR.md`. The token is never written to a log, a URL, or the DOM.

The OAuth device flow is not an option: GitHub's `login/device/code` endpoints send no CORS
headers, so a fine-grained PAT is the only no-backend path.

## Dependencies

| What | Why not hand-rolled |
| --- | --- |
| `js-yaml` | Files are hand-edited and must parse as real YAML — quoting, multiline scalars, flow maps. A subset parser misreads them silently. |
| `rrule` | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` and DST-crossing weeklies are where hand-rolled expansion is wrong without telling you. |

YAML *writing* is ours (~20 lines): we control the output shape, so no dumper is needed.

**Load with `CORE_SCHEMA`, never js-yaml's default.** The default is YAML 1.1 and parses
`start: 2026-04-18` into a JS Date at UTC midnight — silently shifting every all-day entry by a
day east of UTC. `CORE_SCHEMA` keeps it a string and still handles bools, numbers, flow maps and
quoted scalars. This is the same off-by-one the bare-date format exists to prevent, arriving
through the parser instead.

## Platform findings

Verified in both installed home-screen apps (iPhone/Safari, Pixel/Chrome); screenshots in
`spike/res/`.

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Storage shared across paths | **Yes.** A marker written by `/mine/spike/` was read back byte-identical by `/mine/spike/sub/`, both reporting `STANDALONE`. Cross-path module imports work too. |
| `{type:'module'}` service worker | Registers on Safari as well as Chrome. No classic fallback needed. |
| `storage.persisted()` | **Already granted**, no prompt, on both. An installed app is exempt from the ~7-day eviction that applies to uninstalled sites, so the token and mirror survive idle periods. |
| Quota | 35 GB (iPhone), 56 GB (Pixel), against a mirror measured in single-digit MB. |

Not tested, and no longer relevant: whether separately-installed PWAs get isolated storage. That
expectation is why the one-app topology was chosen.

Re-run `spike/` after a major iOS release — two of the four results above contradicted the
documented platform behaviour, and that is exactly the kind of thing that regresses silently.

covers and why it is hand-rolled rather than vendored is in
[REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md#markdown-bodies).

## Bootstrap — 1 request

One GraphQL query returns an app folder's tree **with contents and blob SHAs**, nested to the
depth of the layout:

```graphql
repository(owner:$o, name:$r) { object(expression:"main:calendar") {
  ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
    ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
      ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
        ... on Blob { oid text isTruncated } } } } } } } } } } }
```

- `rateLimit.cost` is **1** however many files return — `entries` is not a paginated connection.
  A 16 MB / 145 file response came back in 6 s without error.
- `Blob.oid` is byte-identical to the REST tree SHA, so this single request also supplies the
  SHAs that pulls diff against and writes send as their base.
- Check `isTruncated`: GraphQL truncates very large blobs and returns `text: null` for binary.
  Fall back to a REST blob fetch for that path.
- An **empty repo** returns `object: null` rather than an error, and `defaultBranchRef: null`.
  Treat it as an empty mirror, not a failure.

**Do not use the tarball.** `GET /tarball/{ref}` 302-redirects to `codeload.github.com`, which
answers `access-control-allow-origin: https://render.githubusercontent.com` — one specific
foreign origin. `fetch()` applies CORS to the final response after the redirect, so it is
blocked, and the preflight an authenticated request needs returns 403. `api.github.com/graphql`
by contrast sends `allow-origin: *` and a 204 preflight allowing `Authorization`.

**A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright.** Not just the ref read — `POST
/git/blobs` itself answers 409 "Git Repository is empty", so there is nothing to build a tree
from. Only `PUT /contents/{path}` can create the first commit. The first queued file goes that
way, and everything after drains normally once a history exists.

## Pull

1. `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{branch}` with `If-None-Match`. A 304 means nothing changed and
   costs no rate-limit quota.
2. On 200: fetch the tree, diff blob SHAs, fetch only changed files, drop deleted paths.

Run on app open and on window focus. Background Sync does not exist in Safari, so all syncing is
foreground.

## Writes — one commit per drain

Queue each change locally with the blob SHA it was based on, then drain the whole queue as one
commit via the Git Data API: `POST /git/blobs` per file, `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`
(deletion = entry with `sha: null`), `POST /git/commits`, `PATCH /git/refs/heads/{branch}` with
the expected old SHA and **no force**.

One drain is one commit, so a move — delete plus create, because the date is in the path and the
API has no rename — cannot be half-applied, and a 20-item offline backlog is one commit.

A rejected ref update means someone pushed elsewhere: pull, rebuild on the new base, retry. This
succeeds, because nearly every write is a create at a freshly generated path.

**True conflict** = a queued change whose base SHA no longer matches the remote blob. Remote keeps
the canonical path; the local version is committed beside it as `<name>.conflict-<yyyymmdd>.md`
with `conflictOf:`. Nothing is discarded and the queue never jams. On 401/403, pause and send the
user to settings.

## Service worker

Registered `{type: 'module'}` so it can import `shared/apps.js`. A version constant names the
cache; install precaches the shell. Same-origin requests are cache-then-revalidate.

Requests to `api.github.com` **bypass the worker entirely** — caching an API response would hand
back a stale ETag and silently break sync.

A new worker waits; the UI offers "Update ready — reload" and `skipWaiting()` runs only on tap.

**The offer is gated on the version, not on a worker waiting.** The worker answers a `version`
message over a `MessageChannel` port with its `VERSION` constant, and the page compares the
waiting worker's answer with the active one's; equal answers mean no banner. A worker that is
byte-identical to the running one can sit in `waiting` indefinitely, and `reg.waiting` alone as
the condition is what makes the banner appear on an app with no update and never go away. A
worker too old to answer reports `null` after a 1.5 s timeout, which differs from a real version
and so still offers the update.

## Token and CSP

Stored plaintext in IndexedDB with its expiry: as safe as the unlocked device. The threat that
matters is injected script on our own origin, closed off by policy rather than encryption:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com
```

**No CDNs, ever.** Dependencies are committed to `/shared/vendor/`, pinned by hand, with source
URL and version in `VENDOR.md`. The token is never written to a log, a URL, or the DOM.

The OAuth device flow is not an option: GitHub's `login/device/code` endpoints send no CORS
headers, so a fine-grained PAT is the only no-backend path.

## Dependencies

| What | Why not hand-rolled |
| --- | --- |
| `js-yaml` | Files are hand-edited and must parse as real YAML — quoting, multiline scalars, flow maps. A subset parser misreads them silently. |
| `rrule` | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` and DST-crossing weeklies are where hand-rolled expansion is wrong without telling you. |

YAML *writing* is ours (~20 lines): we control the output shape, so no dumper is needed.

**Load with `CORE_SCHEMA`, never js-yaml's default.** The default is YAML 1.1 and parses
`start: 2026-04-18` into a JS Date at UTC midnight — silently shifting every all-day entry by a
day east of UTC. `CORE_SCHEMA` keeps it a string and still handles bools, numbers, flow maps and
quoted scalars. This is the same off-by-one the bare-date format exists to prevent, arriving
through the parser instead.

## Platform findings

Verified in both installed home-screen apps (iPhone/Safari, Pixel/Chrome); screenshots in
`spike/res/`.

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Storage shared across paths | **Yes.** A marker written by `/mine/spike/` was read back byte-identical by `/mine/spike/sub/`, both reporting `STANDALONE`. Cross-path module imports work too. |
| `{type:'module'}` service worker | Registers on Safari as well as Chrome. No classic fallback needed. |
| `storage.persisted()` | **Already granted**, no prompt, on both. An installed app is exempt from the ~7-day eviction that applies to uninstalled sites, so the token and mirror survive idle periods. |
| Quota | 35 GB (iPhone), 56 GB (Pixel), against a mirror measured in single-digit MB. |

Not tested, and no longer relevant: whether separately-installed PWAs get isolated storage. That
expectation is why the one-app topology was chosen.

Re-run `spike/` after a major iOS release — two of the four results above contradicted the
documented platform behaviour, and that is exactly the kind of thing that regresses silently.

content.text:
I've read the whole tree, run the baseline (`test/run.sh` → **all checks passed**, exit 0), and mapped the legacy. Two corrections to your premise before I start asking:

1. **`mine-data` isn't in this repo.** The samples live in `calendar/sample/` (6 files), and they're **already on the current format** — `important: true`, `stage:`, no `priority:`, no `done:`. Nothing to migrate there.
2. **There are no unit tests.** `test/` is a single 1131-line browser-driven CDP integration suite. `TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md` argues explicitly against unit tests, while also claiming `buildModel` is pure "so it can be exercised from node" — which nothing does.

What I actually found, grouped:

| | Finding |
|---|---|
| **Back-compat readers** | `priority` (1=important, 2–9=not) and `done:` boolean are read in `data.js`, listed in `popup.js:FORM_KEYS`, seeded in `serve.py`, asserted in `check.mjs`, documented in 4 places |
| **Dead code** | `ui.js:defaultDay()`; CSS `.mode` (the removed `D W M Y K` row), `.gadd`; `#f-path` debug line in the entry popup (not in REQUIREMENTS, not tested) |
| **Duplication** | `pad` ×3, `list` ×2, `weekLetters` ×2 (app.js + views.js), 5 icon SVG paths inlined in `calendar/index.html` that also exist in `ui.js:ICON` |
| **Unreachable architecture** | `github.js:bootstrap/graphql/treeFields/collect` (~45 lines) is used only by the main app's "Verify round-trip" dev button. `pull()` does the real mirroring |
| **Overlay spaghetti** | three mechanisms — `.pop` (anchored by `openPop`), `.sheet` (centred, stale name), `.modal` (flex-centred) — plus `#day-pop` getting `left/top !important` on phones to undo its own anchoring |
| **Documented, never built** | `widget.js` / `summary()` in 3 doc places; `spike/apps.js` still has `widget: true`; `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md` points at `spike/res/` screenshots deleted in `eb80c09` |
| **Real bug** | `sw.js:SHELL` precaches `shared/md.js` but **not** `shared/markdown.js`, which `popup.js` imports |
| **Over-structured** | board filter builds a `pop-sub` heading + `chiprow` + one `chip` for what is now a single toggle |

Starting down the tree.

questions.question: There are three overlay mechanisms: `.pop` (positioned under an anchor by `openPop`), `.sheet` (centred, stale name from the bottom-sheet era), and `.modal` (own backdrop, flex-centred) — plus two scrims. `#sub` carries `.pop` but is overridden to centred in CSS, and `#day-pop` is anchored by `openPop` then forced back with `left/top: 50% !important` on phones. calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md says the day preview is centred, full stop; the CSS comment says "beside the day on desktop". How far do I consolidate?

options.label: Two mechanisms, day-pop centred (Recommended)
options.description: `openPop` keeps only the two real dropdowns (picker, filter). The day preview, the field sub-popup and the settings panel share one centred class, differing only in width. `.sheet` is renamed, the `!important` block and day-pop's anchor lookup go. `.modal` stays for the three overlays that bring their own backdrop. Day preview becomes centred on desktop too — a visible change, and the one REQUIREMENTS.md already describes.

options.label: Same, but keep desktop day-pop anchored
options.description: Consolidate `.sheet` and `.pop.sub` into one centred class and give `#day-pop` an explicit class instead of the `!important` fight, but keep it beside the day cell on desktop and update REQUIREMENTS.md to say so. No visible change; `openPop` keeps three callers.

options.label: Rename only
options.description: Drop the stale `.sheet` name and the `!important`, leave the three mechanisms and the desktop behaviour as they are. Lowest risk against the 320px centring checks.

questions.question: Four duplications: `pad` defined identically in data.js, views.js and popup.js; `list` in data.js and popup.js; `weekLetters` in app.js and views.js (same body, one returns names, the other `[name, isWeekend]` pairs); and 7 icon SVG paths inlined in calendar/index.html that already exist in `ui.js:ICON` (filter, plus, x ×3, trash, disk). The import graph allows `pad`/`list` in data.js and `weekLetters`/`isWeekend` in ui.js with no cycle. options.description: Export `pad` and `list` from data.js, move `weekLetters`+`isWeekend` to ui.js returning pairs (app.js maps to names). One icon table, 7 duplicated paths gone.

content.text: Removing it. Now the test question — and this is where your brief and the repo disagree.

questions.question: You asked me to update the unit tests. There are none: `test/` is `run.sh` + `serve.py` + a 1131-line browser suite driven over the DevTools protocol. TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md has a section titled "Why a browser and not unit tests" — but it carves out an exception: "The model arithmetic that *is* worth testing in isolation (dates, sprints, recurrence expansion) is pure and lives in calendar/data.js, whose `buildModel` takes files rather than reading them, so it can be exercised from node." Nothing does. I verified `calendar/data.js` does import cleanly in node 20 — no top-level IndexedDB or fetch, and `crypto.getRandomValues` is global. What do you want?

options.label: Update the browser suite and add test/unit.mjs (Recommended)
options.description: Required either way: delete the 6 priority/done checks and 2 fixture rows, and extend the day-preview centring check to desktop now that it is centred there. Plus a new ~100-line `test/unit.mjs` over data.js's pure arithmetic — isoWeek, addMonths, sprint maths, occurrence expansion with exdate and override, the two-pass DST instant, and what `entryFile` actually serialises — run by `run.sh` before the browser starts, using the same `ok()` output style. No dependencies, no build step. This is what the doc already promises and what "unit tests" meant.

options.label: Update the browser suite only
options.description: Do the required edits to check.mjs and serve.py and add nothing. Keeps `test/` to one suite and one mechanism, consistent with TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md's stated position; leaves data.js's arithmetic covered only indirectly through the UI.

options.label: Browser suite plus a larger unit layer
options.description: Also cover `shared/md.js` round-tripping and the RRULE round-trip logic — which means first extracting `choiceOf`/`buildRule` out of popup.js, since that file imports ui.js and touches the DOM. More coverage, but it is a refactor beyond removing legacy.

content.text: One genuine bug surfaced, with a design fork behind it.

questions.question: `sw.js:SHELL` precaches `shared/md.js` but not `shared/markdown.js`, which `calendar/popup.js` imports — so a cold-installed app that goes offline before ever opening an entry popup cannot render a details body. It is a hand-maintained list, and so is `shared/apps.js`'s per-app `files` array, which currently lists the calendar's 9 files by name. Both drift silently; this omission is the proof. How do I fix it?

options.label: Add the missing file, keep the lists (Recommended)
options.description: Add `./shared/markdown.js` to SHELL. The lists stay explicit: `install` uses `cache.addAll`, which rejects as a whole if any URL 404s, so a wrong entry fails loudly at install — that is worth more than inferring the list. One line, and the omission is the only one I found.

options.label: Add it and drop the per-app file list
options.description: Add markdown.js, and reduce `shared/apps.js` to slug and label — precaching only each app's folder index and icon and letting cache-then-revalidate pick up the modules on first use. Nothing to keep in sync, but the first offline visit to an app that was never opened online would fail.

options.label: Derive the lists
options.description: Generate the shell list rather than writing it — which needs either a build step or a fetch-and-parse of the import graph at install time. Both are contrary to the repo's no-build-step rule.

content.text:
All branches resolved. The plan, then I'll build it.

**Remove** — `priority`/`done` readers (code, fixture, 6 checks, 4 docs); `github.js` GraphQL bootstrap + its doc section; `#f-path` and its ternary; `ui.js:defaultDay()`; CSS `.mode` (the deleted `D W M Y K` row) and `.gadd`; `spike/apps.js`; the `widget.js` plumbing docs.
**Consolidate** — overlays to two mechanisms, day preview centred everywhere; `pad`/`list` → data.js, `weekLetters`+`isWeekend` → ui.js; 7 inline SVGs → `icon()` at boot.
**Fix** — `shared/markdown.js` into the precache; stale README status and both layout blocks; `spike/res/` pointer.
**Add** — `test/unit.mjs` over data.js's pure arithmetic, run by `run.sh`.

Three things I'm settling myself, so you can veto: I'm **keeping** the board filter's `Important` heading above its one `!` chip (it's the only visible label on a bare glyph), **keeping** the `S` state object with its `render`/`status`/`push`/`reload` slots (it's the documented import-cycle break; replacing it is a bigger change than the mess it removes), and only dropping the `export` keyword — not the functions — from `views.js`'s three file-local helpers.

Success criteria: `test/run.sh` exits 0, every check passing, unit suite included; and no grep hit left for `priority`, `done:`, `bootstrap`, `f-path`, `widget.js`, `.mode`, `.gadd` or `defaultDay`.

`ui.js` holds the state in one object with `render`, `status`, `push` and `reload` as slots the
shell fills in, so a view can ask for a redraw or a background push without importing `app.js`
back and making an import cycle.

`FIELDS` in `popup.js` is built while the module is still evaluating, so anything it calls must
be a function *declaration* — a `const` arrow is still in its temporal dead zone at that point.

## Service worker version

The update banner compares versions rather than merely noticing a waiting worker. The worker
answers a `version` message with its `VERSION` constant; the UI shows "Update ready" only when a
waiting worker's version differs from the active one's. `reg.waiting` alone is not the condition
— a byte-identical worker can wait, and then the banner never goes away.

ok README.md (3 edits)
# Mine

A set of small PWAs that keep your personal data as markdown in a private GitHub repo —
calendar, zettelkasten, diary — so it stays portable and free of vendor lock-in.

**Live: https://maximilianharr.github.io/mine/** — install it to your home screen.

## Docs

| | |
| --- | --- |
| [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) | what the app does and how it behaves |
| [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) | how it is built, and the verified platform findings |
| [TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md](TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md) | what is checked before a change ships, and how |
| [calendar/](calendar/) | the calendar app, with its own pair of docs |

## Layout

```
index.html app.js style.css sw.js manifest.json   the main app
shared/   apps.js store.js github.js md.js        used by every app
          markdown.js prefs.js vendor/
calendar/                                         one folder per app
spike/                                            on-device platform checks
test/                                             the checks: test/run.sh
```

No build step: no bundler, no CI, no dependencies to install. `git push` deploys to GitHub
Pages. To run it locally, `python3 -m http.server` in this folder and open the printed URL.
`test/run.sh` runs the model checks in node and the rest in a headless browser, and installs
nothing either.

Data lives in a **separate private repo**, never in this one. The token is entered once in the
app, stored on the device, and scoped so it can only touch that data repo.

## Status

The main app, the sync layer and the on-device checks are done and verified end to end against a
real repo. The calendar is built — the five views, the kanban, the entry popup and its field
popups, the settings panel — and `test/run.sh` covers it.

Not built yet: the per-app summary above the tiles that [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md)
describes. The tile screen shows tiles only, so opening the calendar is currently the only way
to see what is on today.

that will not shrink, a button that stops being wired when its markup moves, a key written into

is why the bulk of the checks drive the real app.

zone conversion, and what a write actually serialises. It is pure: `calendar/data.js` imports

reads as `done` while its neighbours read as `todo`, that a wall-clock time inside the hour a

and that an empty field is omitted from the frontmatter rather than written as `None`."""),

content.text:
The work is done and verified; one extra screenshot run is still finishing in the background, purely for my own eyes on the day preview. Here's where things stand.

## What changed

**Legacy removed**
- `priority` (1–9 → important) and the `done:` boolean fallback — gone from `data.js`, `popup.js:FORM_KEYS`, `patchOccurrence`, the fixture, the checks, and four documents.
- `github.js`'s GraphQL `bootstrap`/`graphql`/`treeFields`/`collect` (~45 lines) and the Bootstrap step in the Verify button. The doc section is now a short note saying it was built, measured, never wired in, and deleted rather than kept as a second way to do what `pull` does.
- `ui.js:defaultDay()`, CSS `.mode` (the removed `D W M Y K` row) and `.gadd`, the `#f-path` debug line and its 5-line ternary, `spike/apps.js`, and the `widget.js` plumbing docs. Two more exports that nothing imported (`SyncError`, `ROOT`) lost the keyword.

**Spaghetti consolidated**
- **Overlays: three mechanisms → two.** `openPop` now positions only the two real dropdowns; the day preview, field popups and settings panel share `.centred` and `openCentred`. Gone: `.sheet`'s stale name, `#settings-sheet`'s id, and `#day-pop`'s `left/top: 50% !important` undoing the positioning that script had just applied.
- `pad` ×3 → `data.js`; `list` ×2 → `data.js`; `weekLetters` ×2 → `ui.js` alongside `isWeekend`.
- 8 icon SVGs inlined in `calendar/index.html` → empty buttons filled from `ui.js:ICON` at boot, the pattern `#home` already used.

**Fixed** — `shared/markdown.js` was missing from `sw.js:SHELL` while `popup.js` imports it; added, with a version bump so the shell is actually re-precached. README's "the calendar is a stub" and both stale layout blocks corrected.

## Tests

`test/unit.mjs` is new: 93 checks over `data.js`'s pure arithmetic — date and month clamping, ISO weeks across year boundaries, sprint ranges, occurrence expansion with `exdate` and an override, the two-pass DST conversion including the hour a zone skips in spring, and what `entryFile` actually serialises. Run by `run.sh` before the browser starts, no dependencies. It passes under UTC, New York, Kolkata and **Kiritimati (UTC+14)** — the zone where `getDate()` bugs surface.

Browser suite: 3 legacy assertions removed, 2 rewritten to check what the app now writes, plus a desktop centring check for the day preview and a check that the 8 JS-wired buttons actually got their icons.

**`test/run.sh` → 302 checks, 0 failures, exit 0.** Baseline before I started was green too, so that's like-for-like.

Per TEST-REQUIREMENTS' "a check must be able to fail": I put both legacy readers back and watched `a done boolean is not read` and `priority is not read` go red, then removed them again. The suite also caught three wrong expectations of mine while I was writing it.

## Two things to look at

**The day preview now opens centred on desktop**, not beside the cell. That's the one visible change. `calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md` already said every overlay is centred; only the CSS comment claimed otherwise. If you preferred it beside the cell, say so — it's a one-line revert plus a doc sentence.

**The tile summary still doesn't exist.** I stripped the `widget.js` interface from the technical docs since nothing implements it, but left the requirement standing in `REQUIREMENTS.md` and said so plainly in the README's Status. Opening the calendar is currently the only way to see what's on today — which, given that document's own line that "the summary on the tile screen is the reminder", is the real gap in this repo. It's a feature, so I didn't build it.

Nothing is committed.

content.text:
Pushed: `c59839a..e9d3e5e` on `main`. Pages will rebuild in a minute or so.

**One thing to check before anything else.** Your private `mine-data` repo may hold entries created during earlier iterations. Any file still carrying `priority:` or `done: true` will now read differently — `priority: 1` no longer means important, and `done: true` no longer means stage `done` (it reads as `todo`). Nothing is lost or rewritten; those entries just render differently until re-saved. Worth a look at the repo on github.com first. If there are such files, say the word and I'll write a one-off migration.

Then, in rough order of what the headless checks can't tell us:

**1. The update banner.** The worker version went `2026-11-20.1` → `2026-11-23.1`, so the installed app should offer "Update ready — reload" exactly once. After reloading, it must not come back. That whole mechanism is untestable headless and the banner-that-never-goes-away is its known failure mode.

**2. Offline details body** — the actual bug I fixed. Open the app online once after updating, go offline (airplane mode), then open an entry with a markdown body. It should render. Before this commit `shared/markdown.js` was never precached.

**3. The eight re-wired icons.** Filter (top pane), the `+` and `×` in the day preview, the trashcan/disk/×/× in a field popup, and × in settings. They're drawn by JS now instead of being inline SVG. They either all work or the app doesn't boot, but a real browser is a real browser.

**4. Day preview on a wide screen** — if you open it on a tablet or desktop browser it's now centred rather than beside the cell. On a phone nothing changes.

**5. Entry popup** no longer prints the file path at the bottom.

**6. Verify round-trip** (main app → settings) now runs three steps, not four — the GraphQL bootstrap step is gone. It still writes `README.md` to the data repo and pulls it back, which is the only real exercise of the write path.

Send me whatever breaks or looks off and I'll fix it.
